response.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city AS city, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN zip_code z ON m.zip = z.zip_code GROUP BY z.city), shares AS (SELECT city, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_share_above_overall_average FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_all a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Cities are grouped by the city name alone (zip_code.city), so same-named cities in different states are merged; attendance records whose member has no matching zip_code row are dropped by the inner joins.
The 'average share across all cities' is the mean of the per-city shares over all cities with at least one attendance record (equals 1/number of cities).
The averages in the output row are computed over only the cities whose share is above the overall average share.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each distinct zip-code city as a (city, state) pair, so same-named cities in different states are counted separately.
alternatives.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city AS city, z.state AS state, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN zip_code z ON m.zip = z.zip_code GROUP BY z.city, z.state), shares AS (SELECT city, state, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_share_above_overall_average FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_all a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
